London Design Biennale

London Design Biennale

5th edition

Surface Reflections
5-29 June 2025

Somerset House

Discover today’s designers and ideas that will change our world.

London Design Biennale returned to Somerset House from 5-29 June 2025 for its 5th edition, showcasing world-leading design, innovation, creativity and research by exhibitors from across the globe. The three-week international exhibition featured curated installations accompanied by a programme of events, thought-leadership talks, performances and workshops.

The theme for 2025, ‘Surface Reflections’ by Artistic Director Dr Samuel Ross MBE, explored how ideas are fuelled by both our internal experiences and external influences. From sensory installations to radical ideas, visitors discovered a powerful exploration of identity, emotion, tradition, legacy and environment.

London Design Biennale opened daily from 11am-6pm with a special Friday Late on Friday 27 June 2025, including live music, food and drinks and special guests THE HERDS and Hampton University Choir.

Thank you for joining us!

Artistic Director

Surface Reflections

Dr Samuel Ross MBE

Dr. Samuel Ross MBE is the Artistic Director of the 2025 London Design Biennale. The British designer and artist is founder of A-COLD-WALL* and SR_A SR_A, as well as the Black British Artists Grants Programme. Ross has set the theme of ’Surface Reflections’ for 2025, which explores how our ideas are fuelled by both our internal experiences and external influences.

Global Design Forum

'Design and the Invisible' Global Design Forum took place from 10-12 June 2025 at King’s College London. How can we dismantle outdated systems and forge radical new ones? Samuel Ross, Mariana Mazzucato, Kengo Kuma and dozens more of the world’s most exciting designers and thinkers joined us for a series of free talks rethinking the hidden powers shaping our world.

Jury 2025

The London Design Biennale International Advisory Committee and Jury is composed of leading creative experts, with a strong commitment to and appreciation of design. They are responsible for awarding medals to the most significant contributions.
